titleZh: 酒店会员数在涨，为什么前台还是认不出回头客？
titleEn: Membership Is Growing. Why Does the Front Desk Still Fail to Recognise Returning Guests?
summaryZh: 会员注册不等于回头客识别。用身份、偏好、权益和决策权四项检查，加上两周五十位客人测试，修复前台识别链。
summaryEn: Membership does not guarantee recognition. Use identity, preference, benefit and decision-right checks, then test the workflow with 50 returning guests over two weeks.
contentZh:
客人第三次住进同一家酒店，前台仍然问：“您以前住过我们酒店吗？”“先生，请您出示证件。”“没有预订吗？”

这不是一句话说得不够热情，而是一条经营链没有接上。会员报表记录了多少账户，客人体验的却是：酒店能不能在他到店前认出身份、在当班员工手里看见必要信息，并兑现曾经承诺的服务。

会员数上涨，不等于回头客识别能力上涨。酒店若继续只追注册量，得到的可能是一批账户，而不是一批被理解、被服务、愿意再来的客人。

第一处断点：同一个客人变成了多个档案

客人第一次从OTA预订，第二次由公司协议下单，第三次打电话到前台。姓名、手机号、证件或邮箱的记录方式稍有不同，系统里就可能出现三个档案。

前台看到的是“新订单”，而不是“第三次入住”。市场部看到会员注册，预订部看到渠道订单，客房部看到一条偏好备注，却没有人确认这些信息是否属于同一个获得授权的客人。

立即检查的不是会员总数，而是重复档案率：随机抽取下一周预计到店的历史住客，能否在不扩大隐私使用范围的前提下，把同一人的合法身份记录准确合并。

第二处断点：偏好被记录了，却不能用于行动

“喜欢安静”“不要靠电梯”“需要硬枕”看起来都像有价值的信息。但如果没有记录来源、有效期和使用授权，或者员工不知道这条偏好是否仍然适用，信息越多，风险也越大。

有效偏好必须回答三个问题：客人是否明确表达过；本次房态能否满足；不能满足时由谁提前说明。把所有历史备注都展示给所有岗位，不是更懂客人，而是缺少数据边界。

立即检查每条偏好是否能转成一个明确动作。不能转成行动、无法确认授权或已经过期的信息，应停止继续累积。

第三处断点：信息没有进入当班员工的视野

酒店可能知道客人是谁，但信息停在市场部表格、会员后台或经理手机里。真正办理入住的员工只看到当天订单，没有到店前名单，也不知道哪些客人需要核对权益。

识别回头客不能依赖员工“眼熟”。应该在到店前形成一张最小清单：客人身份是否确认、可用偏好是什么、承诺权益是什么、出现冲突找谁决定。清单只显示完成本次服务必要的信息，并在班前交接中明确责任。

立即检查：下一周回头客名单，前台能否在30秒内找到这四项信息。如果做不到，问题不在员工记性，而在信息没有进入工作流。

第四处断点：前台看见权益，却没有兑现权限

会员承诺延迟退房、升级、早餐或欢迎礼，现场却受房态、成本和部门权限限制。前台知道客人有权益，但需要逐级请示；客人听到的便是“系统显示有，但今天不一定可以”。

权益不是营销部写出的一句话，而是一项需要资源边界和替代方案的运营承诺。每项权益至少要写明：什么条件下保证，什么条件下视房态，无法提供时可用什么替代，由哪个岗位直接决定。

立即检查过去两周的权益未履约记录。若多数失败来自权限不清，就先修决策权；若来自资源长期不足，就应调整权益本身，而不是要求前台继续解释。

两周测试：先把50位回头客接住

总经理可以用一个很小的测试判断问题是否值得扩大整改。

由前厅经理抽取未来两周预计到店的50位历史住客。以当前回头客识别率、权益履约率、相关投诉和再次预订意向为基线。到店前完成身份核对，只保留一项合法、必要、可执行的偏好，并明确一项能够兑现的权益。

测试期间不增加会员活动，不用额外折扣掩盖流程问题。每天复盘未识别、未履约和需要经理介入的订单，区分是档案、授权、房态还是权限造成。

两周后，如果识别率和履约率提高，投诉没有增加，说明流程修复有效；若信息更完整却仍无法兑现，说明权益设计和资源条件需要改变；若隐私授权不足，则应缩小信息使用范围，而不是继续合并数据。

会员经营的结果发生在到店现场

会员注册发生在页面上，忠诚关系却要在一次次到店中被证明。一个客人被正确认出、得到有边界的个性化服务、遇到冲突时收到清楚解释，才可能把“我有一个会员账户”变成“这家酒店记得我为什么回来”。

今天的第一步很具体：抽取下一周回头客到店名单，检查前台能否在30秒内确认身份、可用偏好、承诺权益和决策责任人。若这四项还没有连起来，先别急着追下一批新会员。
contentEn:
A guest arrives for a third stay and is asked, “Have you stayed with us before?”

This is not merely an awkward service moment. It reveals a broken operating chain. The membership report counts accounts; the guest experiences whether the hotel can identify them before arrival, put relevant information in front of the employee on duty and deliver the benefit it promised.

Membership growth is not the same as recognition capability. If a hotel manages only enrolment, it may accumulate accounts without building relationships.

One guest has become several profiles

The first stay was booked through an OTA, the second through a corporate account and the third by telephone. Small differences in names, numbers or email addresses can create several records.

The front desk sees a new reservation. Marketing sees a member. Reservations sees a channel booking. No one confirms whether the records lawfully belong to the same person.

The immediate diagnostic is not total membership. Sample the returning guests due to arrive next week and test whether duplicate identities can be reconciled accurately within the guest’s permissions.

A preference exists, but cannot drive an action

“Quiet room”, “away from the lift” and “firm pillow” may appear useful. Yet without a source, permission, validity period and fulfilment check, more information can create more risk.

A usable preference answers three questions: did the guest express it; can the hotel deliver it for this stay; and who explains the situation before arrival if it cannot? Old or unauthorised notes should not be treated as better personalisation.

Each retained preference should translate into one clear action. If it cannot, it should not remain in the active arrival workflow.

Information is stored, but invisible to the shift

The property may know the guest, while the knowledge remains inside a marketing spreadsheet, a loyalty dashboard or a manager’s phone. The employee checking the guest in sees only today’s reservation.

Recognition should not depend on memory. A pre arrival view needs only four items: confirmed identity, one usable preference, the benefit promised and the person authorised to resolve a conflict. Only information necessary for the stay should be shown.

Test whether the front desk can retrieve those four items within 30 seconds for next week’s returning arrivals. If not, the issue is workflow rather than employee attentiveness.

The benefit is visible, but decision rights are missing

Late checkout, upgrades, breakfast, parking or welcome amenities all depend on inventory and cost. A front desk employee may see the entitlement but still need several approvals. The guest hears that the benefit exists “in the system” but may not exist in practice.

Every benefit needs an operating rule: when it is guaranteed, when it depends on availability, what replacement is permitted and which role can decide without escalation.

Review the previous two weeks of failed benefits. If most failures came from unclear authority, repair decision rights. If the resource is repeatedly unavailable, redesign the benefit rather than asking employees to keep apologising.

A two week, 50 guest test

The general manager does not need a large programme to diagnose the problem.

The front office manager selects 50 returning guests expected over the next two weeks. Baselines are current recognition, benefit fulfilment, related complaints and stated repeat intention. Before arrival, the team reconciles identity, retains one lawful and actionable preference, and assigns one deliverable benefit.

No new promotion or discount is added during the test. Each failure is classified as an identity, permission, inventory or decision rights issue.

After two weeks, improved recognition and fulfilment without additional complaints indicate that the workflow is working. Better data without better fulfilment means benefit design or resources must change. Insufficient permission means the information scope should contract, not expand.

Loyalty becomes real at the property

Enrolment happens on a screen. Loyalty is tested at arrival. A guest who is correctly recognised, served within clear boundaries and given an honest explanation when a promise cannot be met has a reason to believe the relationship is real.

The first action is practical: take next week’s returning arrival list and ask whether the front desk can confirm identity, usable preference, promised benefit and decision owner within 30 seconds. Until those four elements connect, acquiring more members will not solve the operating problem.
author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
